liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hey Pocky Way** (2 reviews): Opens the first of five nights at the Garden; played brisk but measured, energetic without overreaching; The opener gets the first set off to a strong start [12][17]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Bobby seems to skip the first verse, or his microphone was off [12]
- **Queen Jane Approximately** (1 review): Otherwise strong Queen Jane has some minor technical difficulties [20]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Listener felt something was missing without Donna Jean [17]
- **Gimme Some Lovin'** (1 other source): A Watchtower tease follows it [1]
- **Black Peter** (1 other source): An All Along The Watchtower tease comes just before it [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **Equipment Problems/Beer Barrel Polka**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-09-15.sbd.miller.76347.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 3.57/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: Flaws in Minglewood and When Push Comes To Shove were fixed in this upgrade [1]
- **gd1987-09-15.nak300.gidley.115933.flac2448**: audience recording; 22 songs; 152 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd87-09-15.schoeps.willy.15388.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 3/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is good but very echoey, which doesn't match how the Garden sounded; Audience recording with crowd noise audible throughout [15][17]
- **gd1987-09-15.154306.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 151 min [5]
- **gd87-09-15.sbd.miller.21981.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 143 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [9]. Said about its sound: High-quality soundboard, but interference and static are present throughout the show [13]

## Around the show

- Attendee says the second set was played cleanly, with no missed notes or lyric stumbles, and Jerry's voice was strong [14]
- Part of the fall east coast tour run, when Brent firmly established himself in the band [13]
- 1987 is called underrated: the band's sound was tighter and bigger, with high-energy full-band jams [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-09-15.sbd.miller.76347.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D6/TDK MA-R90) [1]. Also: Reviewer credits this soundboard copy to a Charlie Miller remaster; Transfers and mastering done at 24bit/48k, then resampled and dithered to 16bit/44.1k using Samplitude, from Steve Marcus's lent masters [1][18]
- **gd1987-09-15.nak300.gidley.115933.flac2448**: taped by Ted Gidley; transferred by AndrewF; source: 24bit/48kHz file set: OTS AUD: 2x Nakamichi CM300 w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90's, w/no Dolby. Taped by Ted Gidley. [3]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source; a patch from another source covers a tape flip during Space [3]
- **gd87-09-15.schoeps.willy.15388.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Willy; source: Audience: Schoeps CMC 44's [4]
- **gd1987-09-15.154306.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [5]. Also: Master cassette from Michael Hessberg, transferred by Charlie Miller, with a 14-second Drums patch from Joe D'Amico's Nakamichi 304 source [5]
- **gd87-09-15.sbd.miller.21981.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (48k) -> Behringer UltraMatch SRC 2000 -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHN - Transfered and Edited By… [9]
